title: Mean under coordinate fixing
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and let $\iota$ be a finite nonempty index set. Suppose the real-valued functions on $\Omega$ have a basis indexed by $\iota$ that contains the constant-one function and is orthonormal for the inner product given by expectation under $\pi$. For any natural number $n$, any function $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, and any coordinate $j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$, the expectation over $\omega\sim\pi$ of the product mean of $f$ with coordinate $j$ fixed to $\omega$ equals the product mean of $f$.
hypotheses_covered: $\pi$ is a probability mass function on $\Omega$
A real basis of functions on $\Omega$ indexed by $\iota$ exists, with one basis vector constant one
The basis is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product
caveat: The statement uses the defined product mean and coordinate-fixing operation; their detailed formulas are not included in the supplied definitions.
